_comment: CALTEX MD Bot - Pterodactyl Egg Configuration. Node.js 20 + tsx + Baileys. Supports three connection modes: (A) auto-connect with local creds, (B) GitHub credential restore (legacy), (C) interactive pairing code flow on Pterodactyl (default on first start). NOT a Java/Minecraft egg — do NOT use server.jar.
name: CALTEX MD WhatsApp Bot
author: Caltex254
description: CALTEX MD - Powerful WhatsApp Multi-Device Bot with AI, Plugin System, Web Dashboard & REST API. Uses Node.js 20 + tsx runtime with Baileys for WhatsApp connection. Supports interactive phone-number pairing directly on Pterodactyl — no separate Render session API or Vercel dashboard required. This is a Node.js egg, NOT a Java/Minecraft egg.

installation.script:
#!/bin/sh
# CALTEX MD Bot - Pterodactyl Installation Script
# The bot files are normally uploaded directly by the user. This script is a
# fallback: if package.json is missing, it clones the repo and copies ONLY the
# bot service (mini-services/caltex-bot/) to /mnt/server/.
#
# The bot is Node.js + TypeScript. NO Java, NO Minecraft, NO server.jar.
# Uses /bin/sh (POSIX) because the install container is debian:bullseye-slim
# but the runtime container (ghcr.io/pterodactyl/yolks:nodejs_20) is Alpine
# and does NOT have bash.

set -e

apt-get update -y
apt-get install -y git ca-certificates

# If package.json doesn't exist, clone the repo and copy the bot service files.
if [ ! -f /mnt/server/package.json ]; then
    echo "[install] package.json not found — cloning CALTEX-MD repository..."
    rm -rf /tmp/caltex
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Caltex254/CALTEX-MD.git /tmp/caltex

    # Copy the bot service files (the actual WhatsApp bot) into /mnt/server/
    # Use 'cp -a .' to include hidden files (e.g. .env.example) but exclude
    # '.' and '..' entries that the '.*' glob would otherwise match.
    mkdir -p /mnt/server
    cp -a /tmp/caltex/mini-services/caltex-bot/. /mnt/server/

    # Also copy the Pterodactyl startup script from the repo root.
    cp /tmp/caltex/pterodactyl-start.sh /mnt/server/pterodactyl-start.sh
    chmod +x /mnt/server/pterodactyl-start.sh

    # Clean up.
    rm -rf /tmp/caltex
    echo "[install] Bot files copied to /mnt/server/"
else
    echo "[install] package.json already exists — skipping clone."
fi

# Make sure the startup script is executable (in case it was uploaded without +x).
chmod +x /mnt/server/pterodactyl-start.sh 2>/dev/null || true

# Pre-create the auth_info_baileys directory so the bot can persist credentials.
mkdir -p /mnt/server/auth_info_baileys

echo "[install] Installation complete."
echo "[install] Bot files are at /mnt/server/ (this becomes /home/container inside the container)."
echo "[install] Dependencies will be installed on first startup via 'npm install' (run by pterodactyl-start.sh)."
echo "[install] BOT_OWNER is optional — if not set, the bot will prompt for a phone number on first start."

variables.name: Bot Owner Phone (optional)
variables.description: Optional. Phone number of the bot owner (international format, no + or spaces). Example: 254712345678. If left blank, the bot will prompt for a phone number interactively on the Pterodactyl console when it first starts. Once paired, credentials are saved and the bot auto-connects on subsequent restarts.

variables.name: Bot Session ID (optional, legacy)
variables.description: Optional. Set to a CALTEX-XXXX-XXXX session ID to restore credentials from GitHub instead of using interactive pairing. Leave blank on first start to use the pairing code flow.

variables.name: GitHub Token (optional, legacy)
variables.description: Optional. Only needed if you want to restore credentials from GitHub (legacy mode). Leave blank for the standard interactive pairing flow.

variables.name: GitHub Repo Owner (optional)
variables.description: GitHub username or org that owns the caltex-sessions repo. Only needed if using GitHub restore mode.

variables.name: GitHub Repo Name (optional)
variables.description: Name of the private GitHub repo where WhatsApp credentials are stored. Only needed if using GitHub restore mode.

variables.name: Bot Name
variables.description: Display name for the bot (shown in WhatsApp as the linked device name).

variables.name: Command Prefix
variables.description: Prefix for bot commands. Use '.' for .menu, .ping etc. Other common values: '!', '/', '#'.

variables.name: Auto Read Messages
variables.description: Automatically mark incoming messages as read.

variables.name: Auto Typing
variables.description: Show typing indicator when processing messages.

variables.name: Anti Link
variables.description: Delete messages containing links in groups.
